translationRepairs: She married Emperor Xuan and bore by concubines Prince Daodu of Hengyang and Prince Daosheng of Shi'an; afterward she bore the Grand Ancestor.
She married Emperor Xuan; Prince Daodu of Hengyang and Prince Daosheng of Shi'an were secondary-born (by concubines); afterward she bore the Grand Ancestor.

In 嫁于宣帝，庶生衡陽元王道度、始安貞王道生，后生太祖, 庶生 marks Daodu and Daosheng as secondary-born (of concubines), while only 后生太祖 attributes maternity to the empress. The original literal's 'bore by concubines' wrongly makes her their mother; the proposed wording restores that distinction.
She called Xiao Daocheng by his childhood name Doujiang and said, "It must be you."
She called the Grand Ancestor by his childhood name and said, "It must be you."

呼太祖小字曰 records only that she addressed him by childhood name; the graph 小字 does not supply the syllables Doujiang. Removing the invented childhood name aligns the idiomatic with the Chinese and with the existing literal.
Her father Chen Zhao was made household minister with the purple-gold seal and posthumously titled Marquis Jing.
His maternal grandfather Chen Zhaozhi was made household minister with the purple-gold seal and posthumously titled Marquis Jing.

The emperor is the implicit possessor in 外祖父肇之, so this is his maternal grandfather; 肇之 is the man's full given name Zhaozhi, not Zhao. The revision preserves the Chen surname supplied by the preceding genealogy and corrects both the relationship and name.
candidateDispositions: Speech-introducing function phrase, not a person name.
